items.title: You need to switch to Linux RIGHT NOW!!
items.description: Show ThreatLocker some love and take control of what runs in your environment. See how ThreatLocker can help you lock down applications and AI tools without getting in the way: https://www.threatlocker.com/networkchuck I installed Arch Linux in one minute and forty seven seconds. Omarchy is DHH's opinionated Linux distro built on Arch, Hyprland and Quickshell, and it is the first time Linux has ever felt like the operating system I actually wanted. I put it on an old gaming laptop, then on Terry (my dual RTX 4090 machine), and I let an AI agent rice the whole desktop while I watched. I talked to DHH about why he built it, and Chris from Typecraft showed me how to stop reaching for my mouse. In this video you'll learn how to install Omarchy on almost any hardware, how tiling window managers and Hyprland keybindings actually work, how to build your own Quickshell plugin with AI, how to game on Linux with Steam and Proton, and how to run Windows inside a container when you still need it. Whether you have never touched Arch or you have been ricing your desktop for a decade, this is the walkthrough from a blank USB stick to a computer that is completely yours. items.title: Your Router Might Be Hacked… Here’s What To Do
items.description: Scammers have AI now, and even the router we build in this video can't stop the scam text that walks straight up to your phone. Bitdefender Scam Radar gives you a heads-up when a scam wave hits your area: https://bitdefend.me/90NetworkChuck The government just banned your home router. Chinese state hackers were living inside consumer routers, so the FCC banned future foreign-made ones. And honestly? Your router was already slow, insecure, and boring. So in this video we replace my editor Mike's router (and yours) with OPNsense: a free, open source router and firewall running on a cheap mini PC. Whole-house ad blocking, encrypted DNS, a real firewall you control. Then I hand the whole thing to an AI agent (Hermes on a Raspberry Pi) to see if it can manage the router for us. Its first job: block an entire country. 🎓 Want to go DEEPER? VLANs, firewall rules, GeoIP country blocking, Suricata IDS, and the hardened version of the AI agent are all in my OPNsense course on NetworkChuck Academy: https://ntck.co/NCAcademy RESOURCES / LINKS: 🛠️ Download OPNsense: https://opnsense.org/download/ 🛠️ balenaEtcher (flash your USB): https://etcher.balena.io/ 📖 The Realtek NIC driver fix (full written tutorial): https://blog.networkchuck.com 🧪 Test your ad blocking: https://d3ward.github.io/toolz/adblock.html 📺 Set up your own AI agent (Hermes): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QQEgIo4Juxg 📺 What is DNS?: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NiQTs9DbtW4 📺 The original (6 years ago): your home router SUCKS!!: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lUzSsX4T4WQ HARDWARE (the recommended devices I promised): 🖥️ Skip the driver headache (Intel i226 NICs): CWWK N100 4-port: https://www.amazon.com/CWWK-PC-4-core-N100-Fanless/dp/B0C1TWLHXK 🖥️ The exact mini PC in this video (Getorli Ryzen 3 5300U, Realtek NICs): https://www.amazon.com/Getorli-Display-Support-Computer-Business/dp/B0GHV7W7F6 🖥️ US-vendor appliance option: Protectli VP2430: https://protectli.com/product/vp2430/ 🔀 Managed switch (for VLANs in part 2): MikroTik CRS310: https://www.amazon.com/MikroTik-CRS310-8G-2S-IN-in/dp/B0CH9NHFHS 📡 Wireless access point: UniFi U7 Pro: https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/u7-pro TIMESTAMPS: 0:00 - The government banned your router (here's the plan) 1:10 - Why you should build your own router 1:50 - The hardware: what can run OPNsense 4:04 - The Bitdefender Scam Forecast (Sponsor) 6:13 - Double NAT vs bridge mode: how to connect it 7:39 - Installing OPNsense (flash the USB, boot, install) 10:42 - No interfaces?? items.title: this Raspberry Pi belongs on your wall
items.description: This video is sponsored by NetworkChuck Coffee. Grab a bag of Default Route (my favorite) and fuel your next build: https://ntck.co/coffee Raspberry Pi sent me the new Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2, the 10 inch portrait version, and I mounted it on my studio wall to run all my Home Assistant and homelab stuff. It is a gorgeous little screen (1200x1920, real IPS, 10 finger touch, 400 nits) and at $80 it is a steal. There is one catch though, and a lot of you are not going to like it: this thing only works on the Raspberry Pi 5 and the Compute Modules. Your Pi 3 or Pi 4 will not work at all. In this video I unbox it, walk through everything that is new versus the old touch display, hit a wall when it powered on and did absolutely nothing (turns out you have to update the firmware on your Pi 5, the EEPROM, before it will recognize the screen), mount it with nothing but a drill and some screws, and finally turn it into a beautiful Home Assistant dashboard using an open source kiosk app called TouchKio. Whether you are building a smart home wall panel, a homelab status board, or you just want your Raspberry Pi to show off what it is doing, this is a really good option. Join the NetworkChuck Academy!: https://ntck.co/NCAcademy RESOURCES / LINKS: 🌐 Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2: https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/touch-display-2/ 🛠️ TouchKio (open source kiosk app): https://github.com/leukipp/touchkio 🏠 Home Assistant: https://www.home-assistant.io/ 🖥️ Proxmox: https://www.proxmox.com/ 📖 Update your Raspberry Pi firmware (EEPROM): https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/raspberry-pi.html ☕ NetworkChuck Coffee (Default Route): https://ntck.co/coffee TIMESTAMPS: 0:00 - Unboxing the new Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2 0:45 - What is new on the 10 inch portrait display 1:50 - The catch: Raspberry Pi 5 and Compute Modules only 2:48 - It powered on and nothing happened 3:16 - The fix: updating your Raspberry Pi 5 firmware 5:55 - Building the Home Assistant dashboard with TouchKio **Raspberry Pi provided the Touch Display 2 for this video, no strings attached. All opinions are my own. items.title: I got inside FIFA’s Secret World Cup Broadcast Network
items.description: Build your next random idea on a Hostinger: https://hostinger.com/chuckfifa I spent two days inside the FIFA World Cup International Broadcast Center (IBC), the temporary network that carries every camera, every replay, every goal from 16 stadiums, and the HBS team even handed me a packet capture of a real match. So we open it in Wireshark: uncompressed ST 2110 video, 150,000 multicast flows, and a failover trick that will make any network engineer smile. 🎓 I asked the crew HOURS of questions that didn't fit in this video, the full behind-the-scenes interviews are on NetworkChuck Academy: https://ntck-ac.co/fifa?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=fifa_world_cup_2026&utm_content=fifa_main_tour RESOURCES / LINKS: 🎮 Play the Backrooms of the IBC (built on a Hostinger VPS with a Hermes agent): https://srv732026.hstgr.cloud 📚 THE SIGNAL — the World Cup networking comic I made for my kids: https://srv732026.hstgr.cloud/comic/ 🛠️ Wireshark (decode packets yourself): https://www.wireshark.org 🌐 Official IBC Tours site: https://ibctours.tv 📺 The Hermes video (the AI agent that built the game): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QQEgIo4Juxg TIMESTAMPS: 0:00 - The World Cup is made in Dallas 1:29 - Following one match: Boston → the IBC → the world 3:06 - How a match gets "made" 1,500 miles from the stadium 4:32 - The fiber (and the red/blue trick) 7:08 - Multicast Martin and 150,000 flows 11:52 - The thing I built at 1AM on a Hostinger VPS 14:10 - The people who make the World Cup 16:07 - Decoding a REAL World Cup match in Wireshark 21:45 - Addie's question: the sound of the ball 23:20 - The stadium, the backup plan, and the teardown 29:30 - A prayer for the stressed FEATURING (huge thanks to the crew who make the World Cup — and this video — possible): 👤 Christoph Barbet — Head of Broadcast Infrastructure, HBS (Host Broadcast Services) 👤 "Multicast Martin" — broadcast SDN / TFC 👤 Alex — Master Control Room Supervisor 👤 Wolfgang Herman — IBC Communications Engineer 👤 Mick — Audio Listener 👤 Anthony & Colin — Layer 1 / Broadcast Support 👤 Steve — Control Systems & Dashboards 👤 Gavin — Stadium Manager, AT&T Stadium **Sponsored by Hostinger SUPPORT NETWORKCHUCK: ☕☕ COFFEE and MERCH: https://ntck.co/coffee READY TO LEARN?? items.title: Fable 5 is back.....run these prompts before July 12th
items.description: Fable 5 — the most powerful AI on earth — got pulled offline by the U.S. government three days after it launched, and it just came back. But for most of us the free window is only a handful of days (through July 7). So I sat down with Daniel Miessler, who's already living inside that window, to figure out the one thing that actually matters: what's worth asking it before it's gone. This isn't about doing bigger tasks. It's about pointing maximum intelligence at your deepest systems — your AI harness, the security of everything you've shipped, and the single hardest question about what you're actually building toward — so the payoff outlasts the window. Think of it like a super-intelligent alien that can only help for a week: you don't send it on errands, you have it rebuild your roads. In this video, you'll learn Daniel Miessler's exact list of meta-prompts to run on Fable 5: how to improve the harness that governs all your AI, how to audit the full attack surface of everything you've deployed, and how to ask the model to tell you what you're really shooting at. Whether you're deep into AI already or just trying not to waste the most capable model on earth, this is the prompt playbook for the week Fable is back. items.title: I was wrong about VPNs
items.description: 🔒 This video is sponsored by NordVPN (#ad). Get the exclusive NordVPN deal + 4 EXTRA months here 👉 https://nordvpn.com/networkchuck — it's completely risk-free with Nord's 30-day money-back guarantee! So… do you REALLY need a VPN? I got sponsored by a VPN to make this video — which means I have to be EXTRA harsh to keep any shred of dignity. So I busted 6 of the biggest VPN myths, no sugarcoating, and by the end you'll know exactly what a VPN is actually good for, what it's NOT, and why I still use one every single day. In this video, you'll learn what a VPN actually does (it just changes what network you appear to be on), why "HTTPS already encrypts everything" doesn't mean a VPN is useless, and how your ISP can still see the sites you visit even with secure DNS — I prove it with a live Wireshark capture. We get into what "no-logs" really means and how to verify a provider you can actually trust (RAM-only servers, independent audits, jurisdiction), why a VPN can NOT make you invisible (cookies, logins, and browser fingerprinting still own you), and where a VPN genuinely shines: the metadata it hides, the dedicated IP that protects you from DDoS and swatting, and the all-in-one security stuff NordVPN bolted on top — phishing/malware blocking and the Hijacked Session Alert that watches the dark web for your stolen login cookies. Whether you're a security practitioner who walked in expecting a shill, or just someone wondering if you should even turn one on — this is an honest, decide-for-yourself breakdown. Grade me in the comments. 1 to 10. Be nice.
